q: Borel's normal number theorem says Lebesgue-a.e. x∈[0,1) is absolutely normal. The ergodic proof uses:
opts: Weyl's criterion for all bases simultaneously
Birkhoff's theorem for the expanding map T_b(x)=bx mod 1: a.e. x is generic for Lebesgue, hence normal in base b
exp: Normality in base b is equivalent to x being generic for Lebesgue under the b-fold expanding map T_b. Birkhoff's theorem (T_b is ergodic w.r.t. Lebesgue) gives a.e. genericity, hence a.e. normality. Repeating for all b gives absolute normality.
